BRIEF STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR DECISION:

1. Briefly stated, accused Santosh Kumar has been sent to face trial with the allegations that on 06.04.2024 at 3:30 PM, near General Ticket Counter, Chandini Chowk, Old Delhi Railway Station, falling within the jurisdiction of PS ODRS, the accused fraudulently or dishonestly induced the complainant, to get him the ticket and seat in the train and induced the complainant to hand over the accused Rs.1,530/- and two mobile phones Make Realmi and Itel, with an intention to gain wrongful gain to the accused and wrongful loss to the complainant and thereby the accused is alleged to have committed offence of cheating punishable u/s 420 India Penal Code (herein after referred to as IPC).

2. Upon completion of investigation charge sheet U/s 173 Cr.P.C. was filed on behalf of the IO and a charge u/s 420 IPC was framed against the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
The matter was listed for prosecution evidence.
3. Subsequently, the complainant Sh. Sohel Rana was summoned in the present matter.
A perusal of record shows that repeated attempts were made to secure the presence of complainant.
Further, attempts were also made to serve the complainant through DCP, however, he could not be served.
Accordingly, he was dropped from the list of witnesses.

Since, as FIR No. 24/2024 PS ODRS State vs. Santosh Kumar Page No. 2 of 4 Digitally signed by MANSI MANSI MALIK MALIK Date:

per the list of witnesses, there was no other witness to the incident, except the complainant Sh. Sohel Rana who could have deposed against the accused and proved the involvement of the accused in the present matter,
therefore, continuing the trial would have been a futile exercise as allegations against accused u/s 420 IPC could not have been proved on the testimony of remaining witnesses.
Accordingly, PE was closed.

4. Since no incriminating evidence came against accused Santosh Kumar, therefore,
his statement U/sec. 313 Cr.PC was dispensed with.
5. Final arguments heard.
Record perused.

In a criminal trial, the onus remains on the prosecution to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts and benefit of doubt, if any, must necessarily go in favour of the accused.
It is for the prosecution to travel the entire distance from may have to must have.
If the prosecution appears to be improbable or lacks credibility the benefit of doubt necessarily has to go to the accused.

7. In the present case, it was sine qua non for prosecution to prove that the accused induced the complainant to hand over Rs.1,530/- and two mobile phones to him with an intention to FIR No. 24/2024 PS ODRS State vs. Santosh Kumar Page No. 3 of 4 Digitally signed by MANSI MANSI MALIK MALIK Date:
2026.01.03 15:39:51 +0530 cause wrongful gain to the accused and wrongful loss to the complainant.
To prove the same, the testimony of the complainant was necessary but as stated he has already been dropped from the list of witnesses.

In view of the facts on file, it is quite clear that not a scintilla has come on the record against the accused as the complainant has been dropped from the list of witnesses and no other eye witness to the incident in question has been examined.
8. Hence, in view of the above said discussion, accused Santosh Kumar is hereby acquitted for the offence u/s 420 IPC.
Ordered accordingly.
Announced and Signed in the Open Court on 3rd January, 2026 (MANSI MALIK) Addl.
